legacy_claim_versions.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 041 (Hyperkähler SYZ and projective-space bases.; papers: Projective-space bases of Lagrangian fibrations; The strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
Under the manuscript geometric hypotheses, Lemma bc:differential-identity supplies eta=sum_j D_j(g t_j eta), with t_j in R and regular smooth-base coefficients of bounded ordinary order.

On the generic smooth family, the Serre-dual relative Frobenius scalar s satisfies psi(m) du=Car(F_*(s m du)); pairing the differential identity with a horizontal Frobenius lift gives s=sum_j D_j(g t_j s).

The manuscript completion and rational field-trace argument is valid under its stated normality, separability, common p-basis, regular-coefficient, and degree less than p hypotheses, without assuming s regular.
Given the retained scalar differential identity and Cartier formula of bc:clearing-test, every closed b admits t in R_b with psi(g t)(b) nonzero.

For every prime p and every finite p-basis field K, additive Cartier coefficient extraction annihilates each coordinate derivative. If R is any subring of K, the derivative-stable coefficient subring A lies in R, psi(r)=Car(s r) lies in R, and s=sum_j c_j partial_word_j(g t_j s) with c_j in A and g,t_j in R, then the explicit element t=sum_j t_j adjoint_word_j(c_j) in R satisfies psi(g t)=psi(1). No regularity of s, completion, normality of R, or extension-degree bound is needed.
Proposition bc:ordinary asserts canonical ordinary coefficient base change for every R-module on each retained chart. This remains unverified beyond the clearing bridge in this mission.

The projective-space manuscript asserts that the normal projective base of a projective Lagrangian fibration from a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kahler manifold is projective space. The full theorem remains unverified.

The strong-SYZ manuscript route requires a full smooth cylinder and a torus with the specified angular marking. The relevant metric_estimates, completion, and rotation constructions are unverified and are outside the clearing implication.

The supplied known-status finding is that Soldatenkov-Verbitsky arXiv:2409.09142v3, Theorems 3.7(v) and 3.8, propagates semiampleness from an already semiample deformation to the specified nef pair; it does not construct an initial semiample deformation. Primary-source attribution remains to be recorded.

assumptions.statement: For a projective morphism of smooth complex algebraic varieties and a polarizable pure Hodge module, the filtered direct image is strict and its cohomology objects are pure Hodge modules; strict support and the right-left/Spencer filtration conventions are those of Section 1.2 and Appendices B.2-B.3.
assumptions.source: Morihiko Saito, A young persons guide to mixed Hodge modules, arXiv:1605.00435v3; locally archived and read.

assumptions.statement: Geometric rational variations supplied by a smooth proper algebraic morphism fall in the category of Proposition 4.2.5 satisfying conditions 4.2.2; Theorem 4.2.6 makes their underlying monodromy representations semisimple.
assumptions.source: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, IHES 40 (1971), pp. 43-45; primary PDF archived and read.

assumptions.statement: If a hyperkahler pair (M,L) has L nef with q(c1(L))=0 and admits a deformation with semiample L-prime, then L is semiample. Theorem 3.7(v) assumes a nonempty semiample Teichmuller component; it does not supply that nonemptiness.
assumptions.source: Soldatenkov and Verbitsky, The abundance and SYZ conjectures in families of hyperkahler manifolds, arXiv:2409.09142v3; primary HTML archived and read.
assumptions.locator: Theorem 3.7(v) and its nonemptiness hypothesis; Theorem 3.8
